faq.body: CopyOdds is an open-source platform for Polymarket traders who want to research wallets, rank smart money, and copy trades with transparent controls.

items.q: What is CopyOdds?
items.a: CopyOdds is an open-source AI trading platform for Polymarket. It helps you discover smart-money wallets, analyze addresses, backtest copy-trading fit, and automate execution.

items.q: How does CopyOdds help with Polymarket trading?
items.a: Instead of chasing headline PnL, CopyOdds ranks Polymarket traders by signal quality, consistency, and risk — then lets you inspect curves before you copy.

items.q: What is smart money on Polymarket?
items.a: Smart money means wallets whose Polymarket activity is worth studying: durable edge, controlled drawdowns, and copy-suitable behavior — not just a lucky streak.

items.q: How does wallet / address analysis work?
items.a: Paste any 0x Polymarket wallet to open PnL curves, drawdowns, win rate, and copy-fit. Address analysis is the research step before automated copy trading.

items.q: Is CopyOdds open source?
items.a: Yes. The web app and backend services are public on GitHub under Apache-2.0, so you can audit, fork, and contribute.

items.q: Can I copy trade Polymarket wallets?
items.a: Yes. After you analyze an address, you can mirror trades with position caps, per-market limits, and other guardrails you control.

backtest.title: See the full performance picture.
backtest.body: Review historical return, drawdown, trade frequency, and consistency before you mirror a wallet. Backtests help separate durable edge from short-term luck.
backtest.insight: A smooth equity curve with contained drawdowns usually signals copy-worthy discipline — not just a lucky streak.

copy.title: Copy trades with guardrails built in.
copy.body: Set max position size, per-market caps, copy limits, and wallet protection before any trade is mirrored. You choose the rules — CopyOdds enforces them on every copy action.

features.title: Max position size
features.body: Cap how much of your balance can be allocated to any single mirrored trade.

features.title: Per-market cap
features.body: Limit total mirrored notional per prediction market within a day so one theme cannot dominate your exposure.

features.title: Copy limits
features.body: Set total copy budget and per-wallet limits so exposure stays within your plan.

features.title: Wallet protection
features.body: Per-user custodial trading wallets with passkey/session login and TOTP-bound withdrawals to protect account access.

partnerGuide.title: CopyOdds Partner Telegram Guide
partnerGuide.subtitle: This page walks you through every Telegram step needed to launch your partner bot and Mini App. When you finish, send us your Bot Token and Referral Code — we handle the rest.

overview.title: What you will complete
overview.body: There are three short stages. Follow them in order — each stage unlocks the next.

bot.title: Create your Telegram bot
bot.body: Register a bot with BotFather, save the token, set name + avatar, and disable Group Privacy.

miniApp.title: Attach a Mini App
miniApp.body: Create a Mini App on that bot and paste the Web App URL we provide.

send.title: Send credentials
send.body: Share your Bot Token and Referral / Invitation Code with support.

part1.title: Create your Telegram bot
part1.intro: BotFather is Telegram’s official tool for creating bots. You will create a new bot, choose a public username, securely store the API token, and disable Group Privacy so Telegram can deliver group messages to your bot.

open.title: Open BotFather
open.body: In Telegram, search for @BotFather. Open the verified account (blue checkmark) and tap Start so the chat can accept commands.
open.tip: If multiple results appear, pick the official BotFather with the verification badge — avoid lookalike bots.
open.caption: Search for @BotFather and open the verified account

create.title: Create a new bot
create.body: In the BotFather chat, send the command below. BotFather will reply and ask you to choose a display name for the new bot.
create.tip: Commands are case-sensitive. Type exactly /newbot with no extra spaces.
create.caption: Send /newbot to begin bot creation

name.title: Set a bot display name
name.body: Enter any display name users will see in Telegram. You can use CopyOdds or a branded name for your audience — this is not the unique username.
name.tip: You can rename the display name later with /setname if needed.
name.caption: Choose a friendly display name
name.imageAlt: Setting the bot display name in BotFather

username.title: Set a unique username
username.body: Choose a unique username that ends with bot (required by Telegram). Example: copyodds_demo_bot. If the name is taken, BotFather will ask you to try another.
username.tip: Usernames can only use letters, numbers, and underscores. Pick something easy for partners to recognize.
username.caption: Username must be unique and end with “bot”
username.imageAlt: Choosing a unique bot username ending with bot

token.title: Save your Bot Token
token.body: When creation succeeds, BotFather sends an API token that looks like the example below. Copy the full token and store it somewhere private — this is what you will send to us.
token.tip: Never post the token in public chats, screenshots shared broadly, or GitHub. Anyone with the token can control your bot.
token.caption: Copy the full API token and keep it private
token.imageAlt: BotFather returning the bot API token

avatar.title: Set the bot avatar
avatar.body: Send /setuserpic, tap your bot name when BotFather asks, then upload the 512×512 avatar below. Do not upload before selecting the bot.
avatar.tip: Use the 512×512 file for /setuserpic. The square site logo (400×400) is too small and the Mini App cover (640×360) is the wrong shape.
avatar.caption: Select your bot first, then upload the 512×512 avatar
avatar.imageAlt: Using /setuserpic to upload a bot avatar

setName.title: Confirm or update the bot name
setName.body: Optionally send /setname, choose your bot, and confirm the display name looks right for your brand before moving on to the Mini App.
setName.tip: This step is optional if the name from creation already looks good.
setName.caption: Optional: refine the display name with /setname
setName.imageAlt: Using /setname to update the bot name

privacy.title: Disable Group Privacy
privacy.body: This step is required after the bot is created (and again after any redeploy if privacy was reset). In BotFather, send /setprivacy, select your bot, then choose Disable.
privacy.tip: If Group Privacy stays enabled, Telegram will not push group messages to your bot — commands and group traffic will look broken even when the token is correct.

part2.title: Create your Telegram Mini App
part2.intro: A Mini App turns your bot into a launch button for the CopyOdds web experience inside Telegram. You will create the app, select your bot, fill in basic metadata, then paste the Web App URL we give you.

create.title: Start Mini App creation
create.body: Stay in the @BotFather chat and send /newapp. BotFather will walk you through attaching a web app to one of your bots.
create.tip: If BotFather says you have no bots, finish Stage 1 first.

select.title: Select your bot
select.body: When prompted, choose the bot you created in Stage 1. The Mini App will be linked to that bot only.
select.tip: If you manage multiple bots, double-check you selected the partner bot — not a personal test bot.
select.caption: Select the bot that will host the Mini App
select.imageAlt: Selecting your bot when creating a Mini App

info.title: Enter app information
info.body: Fill in the app metadata BotFather asks for. You can use the recommended values below unless we provide a custom brand pack.
info.photoNote: When BotFather asks for a photo, upload the 640×360 cover below. Square logos will be rejected.
info.tip: BotFather requires exactly 640×360 for the Mini App photo. Do not reuse the bot avatar file.

url.title: Enter the Web App URL
url.body: We will send you the exact Web App URL for your partner deployment. When BotFather asks for the URL, paste it exactly as provided — do not modify the path or query string.
url.tip: If you do not have the URL yet, message support first. Creating the Mini App shell is fine; the URL can be set once we issue it.
url.caption: Paste the partner Web App URL from our team
url.imageAlt: Entering the Web App URL in BotFather

test.title: Test the Mini App launch
test.body: Open your bot chat and tap Open App (or the menu button Telegram shows). Confirm the Mini App loads correctly before sending us your credentials.
test.tip: If the app fails to open, re-check the Web App URL in BotFather and make sure you selected the correct bot.
test.caption: Verify “Open App” launches the Mini App
test.imageAlt: Opening the Mini App from the Telegram bot

send.title: What to send us
send.intro: Once the bot and Mini App are ready, message Telegram support with the two items below. That is enough for us to finish partner setup on our side.

token.title: Bot Token
token.body: The full API token BotFather returned after /newbot (or from /token if you need to retrieve it again).

referral.title: Referral / Invitation Code
referral.body: Your partner Referral Code or Invitation Code so we can bind traffic and attribution correctly.

send.note: Aside from disabling Group Privacy with /setprivacy → Disable, no other Telegram configuration is required on your side. After we receive both items, we complete backend binding and confirm go-live with you.
send.ctaHint: Send both items in one message so onboarding is faster.

verified.title: Use the verified BotFather
verified.body: Only trust @BotFather with the official verification badge. Fake bots can steal tokens.

username.title: Username must end with bot
username.body: Telegram rejects usernames that do not end with “bot”. Keep a few backup names ready.

token.title: Treat the token like a password
token.body: Anyone with the token can message users as your bot. Store it privately and only share it with our support channel.

privacy.title: Disable /setprivacy or group messages never arrive
privacy.body: Send /setprivacy in BotFather, pick your bot, and choose Disable. Otherwise Telegram will not push group messages to the bot.

url.title: Wait for our Web App URL
url.body: Do not invent a URL. We issue the partner Web App link after reviewing your bot details.

copyTrade.title: Copy Trade Polymarket: How to Mirror Top Wallets Automatically
copyTrade.excerpt: Polymarket has no built-in copy trading. CopyOdds does — discover smart-money wallets, backtest them, and mirror trades with risk controls you set.
copyTrade.subtitle: Polymarket doesn't ship copy trading. CopyOdds uses on-chain wallet data to rank traders, score copy-fit, and mirror fills automatically — with position caps you control.

toc.title: In this guide
toc.body: From whether Polymarket supports copy trading, to how CopyOdds executes, how to pick a wallet, and the risk controls that matter.

canYou.title: Can you copy trade?
canYou.body: Polymarket has no native button — CopyOdds fills the gap.

why.body: Edge exists; timing by hand usually doesn't.

canYou.title: Can you copy trade on Polymarket?
canYou.p1: Polymarket does not include a built-in copy-trading feature. There is no official “follow this wallet” switch inside the exchange UI.
canYou.p2: The data to do it still exists on-chain: every fill is public. <app>CopyOdds</app> is an open-source AI trading platform that ranks those wallets, lets you inspect address-level performance, and mirrors trades automatically inside rules you set — max position size, per-market caps, and copy limits.

why.title: Why copy trade on Polymarket?
why.p1: Polymarket's strongest traders are usually researchers, not lottery tickets. They find events where the crowd's implied probability is meaningfully wrong — then they size in before the market catches up.
why.p2: Finding those wallets is one job. Copying them in time is another. By the time a manual watcher sees a fill and submits their own order, the price has often already moved. Copy trading automates discovery-to-execution so you are not competing with a stopwatch.

how.title: How CopyOdds copy trading works
how.intro: CopyOdds does not blindly chase headline PnL. It scores wallets for signal quality, consistency, and risk, then lets you backtest copy-fit before a single trade is mirrored.

discovery.title: Smart-money discovery
discovery.body: The leaderboard ranks Polymarket wallets by more than total profit: consistency, activity, drawdowns, and risk flags sit next to returns so you can shortlist traders worth following.

analysis.title: AI analysis and backtest
analysis.body: Open any 0x address for PnL curves, drawdowns, and copy-fit. Backtest is the research step — you see how a wallet behaved before you allocate capital.

execution.title: Risk-controlled mirroring
execution.body: When a followed wallet trades, CopyOdds can mirror the action inside your rules: max position, per-market cap, copy budget, and wallet protection.

opensource.title: Open source, inspectable
opensource.body: Frontend and backend are public on GitHub under Apache-2.0. You can audit ranking, copy workflows, and execution instead of trusting a black box.

setup.title: Setting up copy trading on Polymarket via CopyOdds
setup.intro: You can start from the web app or the Telegram bot. Typical setup is under 10 minutes.

open.title: Open CopyOdds
open.body: Launch the <app>web app</app> or open the official Telegram bot at <telegram>@copyodds_bot</telegram>.

account.title: Create your account and fund it
account.body: Sign in and deposit so copy orders have a balance to work with. Review the <trust>Trust Center</trust> for funds, fees, and risk notes before you fund an account.

pick.title: Pick a wallet to copy
pick.body: Browse the <leaderboard>smart-money leaderboard</leaderboard>, or paste any Polymarket 0x address to analyze it — you are not limited to names on the board.

backtest.title: Backtest before you copy
backtest.body: Inspect return curves, drawdowns, win-rate context, and activity. A profitable streak with ugly drawdowns is a different product than a consistent, copy-suitable wallet.

activate.title: Set risk controls and activate
activate.body: Cap max position size, per-market exposure, and total copy budget. Then turn copy trading on — CopyOdds mirrors fills inside those guardrails from that point forward.

pick.title: How to pick which wallet to copy
pick.intro: Headline PnL is a starting point, not a thesis. CopyOdds is built so you can reject wallets that look good on a leaderboard screenshot and fail under a curve.

consistency.title: Consistency over spikes
consistency.body: Prefer wallets with repeatable performance. One outsized win can dominate all-time PnL and still be a poor copy target.

history.title: Enough trade history
history.body: A high win rate on a handful of bets is noise. More trades — and live activity — make the stats meaningful.

trend.title: Recent PnL and copy-fit
trend.body: All-time numbers lag. Check the latest window, drawdowns, and whether the backtest still looks copy-suitable.

diversity.title: Market diversity
diversity.body: Wallets that only sit in one event concentrate risk. Traders who work across categories are usually easier to size around.

risks.title: What are the risks?
risks.intro: Copy trading does not remove market risk — it relocates the research. You are trusting the wallet you follow. Past performance does not guarantee future results, and a strong win rate still means a large share of trades lose.
risks.trustLink: Before you deposit or activate copy trading, review funds, fees, and verification details in the <trust>Trust Center</trust>.

judgment.title: You inherit their mistakes
judgment.body: If the lead wallet is wrong, late, or over-sized, a 1:1 mirror copies that too. Treat copy as a process, not a signal to turn off thinking.

limits.title: Use hard caps
limits.body: Set a maximum position per trade, a per-market cap, and a total copy budget before you activate. CopyOdds enforces those rules on every mirrored action.

diversify.title: Don't copy only one wallet
diversify.body: Following two or three uncorrelated wallets usually beats putting the entire copy budget on a single address.

vsManual.title: The advantage over manual trading
vsManual.p1: Manual Polymarket trading means finding markets, researching outcomes, watching wallets, and executing fast enough to keep a usable price. Copy trading automates the last mile: when a followed wallet trades, the copy can fire inside your limits without you sitting on the book.
vsManual.p2: CopyOdds adds the research layer most copy bots skip — AI scoring, address analysis, and backtest before you subscribe — and ships it <github>open source</github> so you can inspect how ranking and execution work.

items.q: Does Polymarket have built-in copy trading?
items.a: No. Polymarket does not include a native follow-or-copy feature. CopyOdds adds copy trading on top of public on-chain wallet activity, with ranking, backtest, and risk controls.

items.q: How does CopyOdds copy a Polymarket wallet?
items.a: You pick a wallet from the leaderboard or paste a 0x address, review its backtest, set position and market caps, then activate. When that wallet trades, CopyOdds can mirror the action inside those rules.

items.q: Is CopyOdds open source?
items.a: Yes. The web app and backend services are public on GitHub under Apache-2.0, so ranking logic and copy workflows can be audited.

items.q: Do I have to copy a leaderboard wallet?

hero.title: Know how it works before you copy.
hero.subtitle: CopyOdds uses per-user custodial trading wallets, platform Gas for copy usage, and TOTP-bound withdrawals. Read how funds, fees, and risk controls work before you deposit.

funds.title: Each user gets an independent custodial trading wallet
funds.body: An independent address does not mean non-custodial. CopyOdds still executes copy trades through a backend signing service, and withdrawals follow the live authorization, address checks, and step-up verification rules. You do not connect MetaMask or import a private key. Each user gets a dedicated execution address and Polymarket Deposit; trading collateral sits in Deposit / pUSD on Polygon.
bullets: One user, one custodial execution address and one Polymarket Deposit — mirrored trades use your account, not a shared platform hot wallet.
You do not custody or export the trading private key. Signing is performed by a separate wallet service for Relayer message / typed-data flows — not arbitrary raw transaction signing.

On Polygon, USDC.e sent to your custodial address auto-forwards to Deposit and wraps to pUSD; native USDC / USDT0 / Wormhole USDT auto-route via Polymarket Bridge to pUSD. BSC deposits must use the Bridge EVM address shown for that network (same address used by verified-deposit messaging) — do not send BSC assets to the custodial EOA.
CopyOdds support will not ask you to disclose a private key, recovery phrase, or authenticator codes.
This is still custodial: the platform can sign copy trades on your behalf. That is different from a non-custodial wallet where keys stay only on your device.

deposit.title: Deposit to your custodial address
deposit.body: Open a custodial wallet in the app, then fund the Polygon custodial address shown there; for BSC deposits use the Bridge EVM address. Trading collateral lands in your Polymarket Deposit as pUSD.

allocate.title: Set ratio or fixed size and risk caps
allocate.body: Choose RATIO or FIXED_AMOUNT sizing, then set max notional, per-market caps, daily caps, slippage, and other subscription guards before activation.

execute.title: Mirrored trades use your Deposit
execute.body: When a followed wallet fills on Polygon, CopyOdds can mirror the action through your per-user CLOB client inside those rules. Fills, slippage, and misses can still differ from the leader.

withdraw.title: Withdraw with TOTP to your address
withdraw.body: Withdrawals move Deposit funds to a Polygon address you specify. You must enable an authenticator (TOTP) and confirm this withdrawal’s destination and amount. Open orders, open positions, or an in-flight withdrawal can block the request.

funds.privacyLink: Also read Wallet and Private Key Security in the <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy> for credential and irreversible-transaction wording.

transparency.title: How discovery, mirroring, and research differ from live results
transparency.body: Signals come from on-chain OrderFilled events for followed wallets. Live sizing is ratio or fixed-amount against your Deposit balance, with subscription risk checks — not a guarantee of matching the leader’s PnL.

discovery.title: Smart-money screening
discovery.body: The leaderboard ranks Polymarket wallets using more than headline PnL — including consistency, activity, drawdowns, and risk context — so you can shortlist addresses to research.

signal.title: Signal to execution
signal.body: A block listener watches Polygon CTF Exchange fills for subscribed leaders, then the copy worker sizes and submits orders through your own CLOB credentials after any configured delay.

sizing.title: RATIO and FIXED_AMOUNT
sizing.body: RATIO uses a fraction of your available Deposit USDC/pUSD; FIXED_AMOUNT targets a dollar notional at the leader price. Always set hard caps — following a wallet also inherits late entries and oversized bets.

risks.title: Delay, slippage, misses, and loss
risks.body: Default copy slippage is 5%. Orders may bump to a minimum notional, skip on risk checks, partially fill, fail, or lose money even when the leader looks profitable. Copy trading relocates research — it does not remove market risk.

backtest.title: Backtest vs live copy
backtest.body: Wallet analysis and research curves on this site are screening aids. Live copy PnL is tracked from your mirrored lots and can diverge from both the leader and any historical curve. Past performance does not guarantee future results.

fees.title: Platform Gas points, market fees, and withdrawals
fees.body: Two different costs: platform Gas points are CopyOdds’ in-app billing unit for copy-service fees — not blockchain network gas (such as MATIC / BNB). Polymarket market fees are also external.

platform.title: Platform Gas points (copy service fee)
platform.body: CopyOdds copy-service fees are calculated on qualifying live filled notional and deducted as platform Gas points. Under the current rules (0.5% of notional at 100 Gas points per USDC), a 100 USDC filled notional costs 50 Gas points ≈ 0.5 USDC. Buy Gas packages in the app; real copy requires gasBalance > 0. Applicable Polymarket market fees and network fees are separate.

gas.title: Blockchain network fees and market fees
gas.body: Network fees (e.g. MATIC on Polygon, BNB on BSC) are charged by the chain, not as platform Gas points. Polygon deposit forwards and Relayer steps are usually handled in-product; BSC bridge deposits still need source-chain network fees from your external wallet. Some Polymarket markets also charge taker fees, separate from platform Gas points.

timing.title: When platform Gas points are deducted
timing.body: Buys and sells are charged after an actual fill on filled notional; partial fills charge the filled portion, and later fills of the same resting limit are not charged again. Unfilled, failed, or cancelled orders do not spend platform Gas points. Manual redeem charges after a successful on-chain redeem. Gas packages credit after fulfillment; this is not monthly subscription billing.

withdraw.title: Withdrawals
withdraw.body: The current product does not charge a separate platform withdrawal fee and does not charge a performance / profit-share fee. Funds leave Deposit via Relayer / Bridge to your Polygon native USDC destination after TOTP authorization. If a withdrawal is delayed or blocked, contact official support with the app references — this site does not promise a fixed processing window.

faq.title: Questions to settle before you fund or copy
faq.body: Answers below follow the live custodial + Gas product model used by the trading services.

items.q: Is CopyOdds custodial or non-custodial?
items.a: Custodial. CopyOdds provisions a per-user trading wallet and signs copy orders through a remote wallet service so automation can run without MetaMask. That is different from a non-custodial product where private keys stay only on your device.

items.q: Who controls wallet signing permissions?
items.a: Trading signatures are produced by the platform wallet service for Relayer typed-data / message flows tied to your custodial account. External wallet bind, key import, and direct EOA withdraw are disabled. Outbound transfers without a withdraw authorization are limited to allowlisted destinations.

items.q: Can copy trading lose money?
items.a: Yes. Copy trading does not remove market risk. Leaders can be wrong, late, or oversized; your subscription can still lose. Past performance and strong win rates still include many losing trades.

items.q: Why can my result differ from a leader's result?
items.a: Latency, default slippage, ratio vs fixed sizing, minimum notional bumps, risk skips, partial fills, and Gas pauses can all diverge from the leader. Research curves on this site are not execution-level copy guarantees.

items.q: What fees will I pay?
items.a: After you buy platform Gas packages, qualifying live fills spend platform Gas points at 0.5% of filled notional (100 Gas points per USDC; e.g. 100 USDC → 50 Gas points ≈ 0.5 USDC). Platform Gas points are an in-app billing unit, not blockchain network gas. Unfilled, failed, or cancelled orders are not charged. Some markets also have Polymarket taker fees and network fees. Partner commissions are not your trading fees. The current product does not charge a performance fee or a separate platform withdrawal fee.

items.q: How can I verify a transaction?
items.a: Use the custodial address, Deposit address, and any transaction hashes shown in the app on Polygonscan (and Polymarket profiles for research wallets). Blockchain data for those public addresses is independently inspectable.

items.q: What should I do if a withdrawal is delayed?
items.a: Confirm TOTP is enabled, there are no open orders or positions blocking withdraw, and no in-flight withdrawal. Then contact official Telegram support (t.me/oddsFine) or WhatsApp with your account identifiers and app references. This site does not publish a guaranteed processing SLA.

cta.body: Open the app to fund your custodial wallet, buy Gas, and configure copy controls — or talk to official support if something about funds or withdrawals looks wrong.
